pages.opener: A labour colony from SAMAN is a complete worker housing site delivered as finished buildings, not a kit of parts. Each building is a newly fabricated steel structure from our Bengaluru and Greater Noida facilities, supplied in the six approved building sizes, 60x24 ft G+1 at the small end and 120x24 ft G+2 at the large, sleeping 58 to 216 workers each on the standard planning basis. Dormitory blocks pair with toilet and bath blocks, kitchens and site services to the approved site plan. Pricing is ex-factory against one flat square-foot rate, so every configuration prices the same way and a fixed quote arrives within 48 hours.

rte.heading: Why the colony page and not a single building
rte.body: This page carries the whole worker housing site, dormitory buildings plus the toilet blocks, kitchens and services that make a colony liveable, so a contractor plans the site once instead of buying buildings one at a time. Every building on it is newly fabricated steel in the six approved configurations. Choose it when your brief is the site, not one block.
rte.comparison: Need only one open sleeping hall rather than a full site? The Labor Sheds page carries that single-hall building.

pages.opener: A labour shed is the open-hall version of SAMAN worker housing: one clear sleeping hall per floor with central aisles, built as a light portal-frame steel building with PPGI cladding and high-level ventilation. It suits contractors who need the highest bed count per rupee and manage the hall as one space. The hall comes in six sizes, 60x24 ft G+1 up to 120x24 ft G+2, sleeping 58 to 216 workers a building. The hall is priced ex-factory on one per-square-foot rate, delivered in 7 to 21 working days with zoned lighting and emergency circuits fitted.

rte.heading: Why choose the shed over the room block
rte.body: The shed puts every bed into one open hall per floor, which is the cheapest way to house a large crew and by far the easiest arrangement to supervise as a single space. Fire exits, zoned lighting circuits and high-level ventilation are all sized for open-hall occupancy rather than for individual rooms. Choose it when bed count per rupee matters more than room privacy.
rte.comparison: Crews that need lockable individual rooms are better served by the Labor Hutments room block, and the full worker housing range shows where each build fits.

pages.opener: A labour hutment is the room-based member of the SAMAN worker housing range: a linear block of individual sleeping rooms, each with its own personnel door, aluminium sliding window, fans and a small distribution board. Crews get lockable rooms rather than one shared hall, which suits mixed gangs and longer postings. The block is a welded or bolted MS structure with an insulated corrugated exterior, built in six sizes between 60x24 ft G+1 and 120x24 ft G+2 that house 58 to 216 workers. Every size is priced ex-factory on a single square-foot rate.

rte.heading: Why choose rooms over an open hall
rte.body: The hutment divides each floor into individual sleeping rooms with their own doors, windows, fans and distribution boards, so mixed gangs, supervisors and longer-posting crews get privacy and lockable space that an open hall cannot offer. The trade is a lower bed count per floor at a slightly higher rate. Choose it when room separation matters on your site.
rte.comparison: If maximum beds in one supervised space is the priority, the open-hall Labor Sheds building houses more per floor; see every colony building compared before you choose.

pages.opener: A prefab labour camp is the relocatable build in the SAMAN worker housing family: bolted light-steel panels on pedestal footings, with repeatable door and window modules and plug-and-play electrical blocks, so the same camp dismantles and re-erects at the next project. Blocks arrange around a central services spine to the approved site plan. Sizes span 60x24 ft G+1 through 120x24 ft G+2 for 58 to 216 workers a building, each priced ex-factory on the camp's own square-foot rate with a fixed quote in 48 hours.

rte.heading: Why choose the relocatable camp build
rte.body: The camp is engineered to move: bolted panel joints, pedestal footings and plug-and-play services mean the same buildings dismantle at one project and re-erect at the next instead of being written off. It costs slightly more per square foot than the fixed shed and repays it the first time the camp relocates. Choose it when your projects move.
rte.comparison: If the housing stays on one site for its whole life, the Labour Colony configuration is more economical, with fixed and movable options side by side on the range page.
